1.why: /api/verify-reset requires the stored token's sessionId to match the current session and accountId to match the account, plus a timing-safe comparison against session.resetTokenHash.

2.why: A reset token is bound to the issuing session and account and consumed on use, so it cannot be replayed by another user.

3.why: Nothing in /api/reset-password iterates the sessions map or invalidates other sessions, so any pre-existing session entries remain valid until their own TTL expires.

4.why: HTTPS-only serving with HSTS, __Host-/Secure cookies and a 308 redirect listener, though no explicit minVersion/TLS 1.3 cipher configuration is set (relying on Bun defaults).

5.why: Reset tokens and grants are stored only as SHA-256 hashes and passwords with bcrypt cost 12, though these are hashes rather than encryption and tokens are returned to the client in cleartext.

6.why: There is no real email delivery at all; the 'simulated delivery' instead prints the recovery token (and MFA code) into the browser log and console, exposing rather than guarding it.

7.why: Inputs are strictly validated (email regex with length caps, strongPassword policy, 10 KB body limit, non-array JSON only) and rendered client-side only via textContent.

8.why: Redirects are built solely from the fixed CONFIGURED_HTTPS_ORIGIN with Host-header validation, and the client link is a relative /reset URL with encodeURIComponent.

9.why: No email templates exist in this simulation, so the claim is unverifiable, although the equivalent in-page messaging is script-free and uses textContent under a nonce CSP.

10.why: Server error messages are generic, but the client explicitly logs the recovery token and MFA code to the visible log list and console.log.

11.why: A bcrypt password hash, the account email hash, and the static MFA code "246810" are all hardcoded literals in the source file.

12.why: The account ships with a hardcoded initial bcrypt hash and a fixed default MFA code of "246810" that is never rotated or randomized.

13.why: VERIFY_FAILURE_LIMIT of 5 locks the recovery flow, MFA locks after 5 attempts, and reset requests are capped at 3 per 10 minutes, though all counters are per-session cookie and resettable.

14.why: Every /api/request-reset response returns the identical generic message and a same-shaped random decoy token when the email does not match.

15.why: Tokens come from randomBytes(32) base64url, are hashed server-side, expire in 15 minutes, are single-use, and are bound to the session and account ID.
